method: refero MCP (mcp__refero__refero_search_styles + refero_get_style), probe fired in audit Phase 0, full styles retrieved

references.title: Langbase
references.whatTheyDoBetter: Two-level text-color discipline (Canvas White #fafafa + Ash Gray #a1a1aa only) — stardust.style runs a 5-step dust alpha ramp (72/50/30/15/8%) that dilutes hierarchy; Langbase also frames sections with faint structural grid lines instead of relying on spacing alone.

references.title: Eraser
references.whatTheyDoBetter: Role-based type scale (caption/body/subheading/heading/heading-lg/display, 6 sizes) and a strict radius vocabulary (16px cards / 8px elements / 4px buttons) — stardust.style's scale is ad-hoc across 10 sizes with no consistent ratio (T-scale); Eraser also owns a distinctive display face (National 2 Condensed) where stardust rides the SF Pro system stack.

references.title: Metaview
references.whatTheyDoBetter: Single-vivid-accent discipline (Mint Glare #7affb4 reserved exclusively for primary CTAs) — stardust.style splits its amber identity across three values (#e8b95e / #ffd98a / #854f17) with text-only/background-only role imbalance (T-color-imbalance), so no one amber is unambiguously 'the action color'.

sharedPatternNote: All three references pair the dark canvas with an ownable display face and a tight token vocabulary; stardust.style's distinctive assets are its cream-on-ink inversion sections, the mono eyebrow labels, and the star glyph — underused as system, per audit findings.
